source.author: verg
source.text: Ut quondam Creta fertur Labyrinthus in alta parietibus textum caecis iter, ancipitemque mille viis habuisse dolum, qua signa sequendi falleret indeprensus et irremeabilis error; haud alio Teucrum nati vestigia cursu impediunt texuntque fugas et proelia ludo, delphinum similes, qui per maria umida nando Carpathium Libycumque secant, luduntque per undas.
source.text_original: Ut quondam Creta fertur Labyrinthus in alta / parietibus textum caecis iter, ancipitemque / mille viis habuisse dolum, qua signa sequendi / falleret indeprensus et irremeabilis error; / haud alio Teucrum nati vestigia cursu / impediunt texuntque fugas et proelia ludo, / delphinum similes, qui per maria umida nando / Carpathium Libycumque secant, [luduntque per undas.]
source.text_english: As once in lofty Crete the Labyrinth is said to have had by its blind walls a path woven in, and a twofold trick of a thousand ways, so that the untraced and returnless maze might mislead the marks to be followed; in no other fashion do the sons of Teucrum hinder their tracks by their running, and interweave flights and battles in sport, like dolphins, who, swimming through the wet seas, cleave the Carpathian and Libyan waters and play across the waves.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: De quo et in alio loco idem poeta decantat: Ut quondam Creta fertur labyrinthus in alta: Parietibus textum caecis iter, ancipitemque Mille viis habuisse dolum, qua signa sequendi Falleret indeprensus, et irremeabilis error.
reuse.text_original: De quo et in alio loco idem poeta decantat: Ut quondam Creta fertur labyrinthus in alta: Parietibus textum caecis iter, ancipitemque Mille viis habuisse dolum, qua signa sequendi Falleret indeprensus, et irremeabilis error.
reuse.text_english: Of this the same poet sings in another place as well: Just as once in lofty Crete, as it is said, there was a labyrinth: a path woven among blind walls, and a twofold deceit, having a thousand ways, by which the signs for following would be deceived, with no possibility of capture, and an error from which there was no return.
